records.name: Guiding Stars
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that runs youth programs on health and fitness, career and college readiness, and juvenile justice awareness.
records.what_you_do: Young people take part in fitness and nutrition lessons, career exploration, resume and interview practice, college application help, and financial literacy classes.

cost.text: Not published on the pages read

first_step.how: Email info@guidingstars2014.org or use the contact page to ask how a young person can join a program
first_step.basis: The site does not explain sign-up steps, ages served, or cost, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Site is working but undated, so probably_active. The IRS list gives the street address as 5226 30 Ridge Ave storefront; the site does not give a number, so confirm before use. Legal name on the IRS list is Guiding Stars an Anthony C Richardson Lee Foundation. The site describes its own youth programs, so it is treated as an operating nonprofit, not a grantmaking private foundation; the owner may want to confirm. Eligibility, ages and cost are not published. The site lists a C2L-PHL menu item with no details (see leads_only).

records.name: Italian Folk Art Federation of America
records.notes: National federation for Italian folk arts. Its PO box is in Philadelphia, but the site lists no Philadelphia programs or meetings. Newest dated item is a 2019 conference with no month given; the site's 2017 copyright is not counted. A join page exists at ifafa.us/join-us/.

records.name: Northeast Squeeze-In
records.notes: Volunteer-run retreat for free-reed musicians. The 2026 event (Sept 25 to 27) and the events booked through 2030 are held at Wisdom House in Litchfield, Connecticut, not in Philadelphia. The IRS address is in Philadelphia, so the organizers may be local. Marked out of area; revisit only if the owner wants out-of-state events listed. The site has a contact page but no email or phone on the page read.

records.name: Peace Islands Institute Pennsylvania
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that brings people of different faiths and cultures together through interfaith dinners, a youth academy, cultural exchange trips, and public awards.
records.what_you_do: Come to an interfaith dinner or gathering, the cultural celebration day, or the public heroes event, or sign up to volunteer, intern, or sponsor through the site.

schedule.text: Several events a year, including an Annual Interfaith Iftar, a cultural celebration day, and a public heroes awards event; dates for each are posted on the site

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter or fill in the volunteer form on the site, then watch for the next interfaith dinner or cultural event
first_step.basis: Public events are announced on the site and there are online forms to volunteer or subscribe, though the site does not describe what a first visit is like.

records.notes: Two office addresses appear on the site, one in the header and one in the footer; both are listed, and the site does not say which is current. The newest dated post is from October 2025, which keeps status active for now. The annual interfaith iftar at City Hall is listed without a date. Annual reports for 2023 and 2024 are linked from the site.

records.name: Project S.A.V.E.
records.summary: A Philadelphia-area nonprofit that supports people affected by sexual violence, partner violence, and trauma with advocacy, counseling, peer support, and wellness groups.
records.what_you_do: Join a drop-in healing and wellness group, a virtual peer support group for survivors, or a teen group, or text the support line to ask about services.

schedule.text: Drop-in Creative Healing and Community Wellness Group, 6 to 7:15 pm, June to November 2026; a teen group and a virtual 13-week support network ran in summer 2026

cost.text: Many services are free for eligible people, with sliding-scale fees for others

first_step.how: Text 215-703-8441 to ask for support, or come to the drop-in Creative Healing and Community Wellness Group at 3300 Henry Ave
first_step.basis: A drop-in group and a text line make the first step simple, though the site does not describe intake for counseling.

records.notes: Founded 2016 per the site. The events page lists upcoming items: a women-only Day of Defense on Oct 17, 2026 (free, with a $25 suggested donation) and a community event on Oct 24, 2026 at Lucien Blackwell Community Center. The published phone number is the text line for support. The newsletter form and the Hours section on the site look unfinished.

records.name: Roxborough Manayunk Conservancy
records.summary: Volunteers who look after more than 100 acres of neighborhood parks and trails across Roxborough and Manayunk, with weekly work sessions.
records.what_you_do: Pull invasive plants, plant, clean up, and help maintain trails at weekly volunteer sessions. Tuesday mornings use hand tools and prefer some gardening experience; Tuesday evenings welcome all experience levels.

schedule.text: Tuesday morning hand-tool sessions, 8:30 to 10:30 am; Tuesday evening sessions (the October 2026 evening session ran 5:45 to 7:30 pm). The morning crew returns in spring 2027, and weekend sessions are to be posted later.

first_step.how: Sign up through the Volunteer Events page, then meet at the spot listed for the next session
first_step.basis: Evening sessions are open to all experience levels with tools and guidance provided, and the site explains how to sign up.

records.notes: The IRS list gives the legal name as Roxborough Conservancy; the site uses Roxborough Manayunk Conservancy. The site mentions a newsletter sign-up and a Park Friend program with no details. No email or phone was found on the pages read; a contact page exists at /contact-us and was not read.

records.name: Roxborough Manayunk Wissahickon Historical Society
records.summary: A local history group that keeps an archive of Roxborough, Manayunk, and Wissahickon records, writes neighborhood history, and helps other local groups share their own history.
records.what_you_do: Visit the archive or ask for research help, read the history blog, come to talks and events, or become a member and volunteer.

schedule.text: Meetings and events are listed under the site's Meetings and Events section; no upcoming RMWHS date was shown on the page read

cost.text: Membership is $10 for students, $20 for individuals, or $30 for families

locations.label: Address on the IRS list (confirm the current address on the site)

first_step.how: Become a member (fees above), or use the contact form at rmwhs.org/contact-us to ask about meetings and volunteer work
first_step.basis: The site invites new members and volunteers and the fees are low, though meeting times were not shown on the page read.

records.notes: Dated items include an August 2026 state honor for the archivist and a September 2026 post about a veterans vigil. Two posts say 2026 with no month. The site text is cut off in the read, so later pages may hold more. The site links the Roxborough Male Chorus and the 21st Ward 4th of July Association as groups it helped set up; both are now records of their own.

records.name: Roxborough Ridge Runners
records.summary: A car club serving Roxborough and nearby neighborhoods, with summer cruise nights and car shows open to all makes and models, plus monthly member meetings.
records.what_you_do: Bring your car or come to look at others at a Thursday cruise night or a spring or fall show. Monthly meetings share car maintenance tips and plan community projects.

schedule.text: Summer cruise nights on Thursdays from April to November, weather permitting, starting around 5 pm; monthly membership meetings on the second Wednesday at 7 pm; a spring show on May 16, 2026 and a Toys for Tots show on Nov 7, 2026

cost.text: No cost stated for cruises or shows; membership terms not found

locations.label: Ivy Ridge Shopping Center (summer cruise nights)

first_step.how: Come to a Thursday cruise night at Ivy Ridge Shopping Center, where no sign-up is mentioned, or to the second Wednesday meeting at 7 pm at Adam Kowalski Post, 504 Hermit St
first_step.basis: The site mentions no registration for cruises or shows, so a newcomer can simply come along; membership details were not found.

records.notes: Despite the name, this is a car club, not a running club. The IRS legal name is Roxborough Ridge Runners Inc. The cruise page does not give a year. Membership terms are on a join page that was not read. The Toys for Tots show is run with the partners listed in leads_only.

records.name: Roxborough Turners
records.summary: We could not find a current public page for this club, so what it does today is not yet known.
records.notes: The batch website field held 9139, which is not a web address, so it was treated as missing. One search for Roxborough Turners Philadelphia returned only historical archive records and no current site, events or contact. A search summary of a Historical Society of Pennsylvania catalog record mentioned a 2004 note saying the club was active at 418 Leverington Ave. That catalog page returned HTTP 403 when fetched, so the note is unverified and is not used as a sign of life. The name and search summary point to a German gymnastics heritage club (Turnverein tradition); categories are left blank until a public source confirms it. Held back on purpose: no public source yet, so no categories, audience or sources. The EIN appears in IRS 990-N filings, which does not count as activity under our rules. The contact name on the IRS list is not recorded.

records.name: Schuylkill Dragons
records.summary: A women's dragon boat team founded in 2001 that paddles on the Schuylkill River and trains year round, with paddlers from their 20s to their 80s.
records.what_you_do: Take the five-week Intro to Paddling class in late spring. If invited to the team, join practices on the water and winter workouts.

schedule.text: Practices on Tuesdays and Thursdays from about 6:15 to 7:30 pm and Saturdays 9 to 10 am, April to October, with early Wednesday mornings added in midsummer. Winter has weight training and indoor paddling on Saturdays.

cost.text: $150 for the five-week Intro to Paddling class; yearly dues are prorated for members who are invited to join

locations.label: Dragon boat dock, West Fairmount Park

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on the Join Us page, then register for the Intro to Paddling class when registration opens, usually in April
first_step.basis: No experience is needed, and the site names a five-week beginner class as the way in, with a clear sign-up step.

records.notes: No dated news or races found. The site has a 2026 race calendar heading with no races listed, so status is probably_active. The intro class page does not give a year. The site says it looks for fit, coachable women willing to learn and possibly compete, and that members need a solid base of fitness. The team also bills paddlers for festival participation at season's end.

records.name: Tombe
records.notes: US-registered nonprofit whose work is solid waste management in Zambia and other countries in southern and eastern Africa. The IRS address is in Philadelphia, but no Philadelphia program or meeting was found. The only dated item is a 2024 launch video with no month shown, so status is unknown rather than dormant.

records.name: Wissahickon Sustainability Council
records.notes: Hidden as private. This is the green committee for the Cook-Wissahickon School community (native meadow, schoolyard depaving, outdoor classroom), formed in 2008. The site says members include parents, teachers and neighbors, but the only sign-up it describes is the school's outdoor classroom program, and no volunteer or public joining route is given. The owner may want to reconsider if neighborhood volunteering at the meadow should be shown. Site news and events are undated, so status is probably_active. Mailing address on the site: P.O. Box 26021, Philadelphia 19128. Social links (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram) not recorded.

records.name: Anns Helping Hand
records.summary: We could not find a public page for this group, so what it does is not yet known.
records.notes: The batch website field held a name, not a web address, so it was treated as missing. One search for Anns Helping Hand Philadelphia found no Philadelphia group by that name. The results were other organizations: Helping Hand Rescue Mission (610 N 6th St, a different group), an Illinois group called Ann's Helping Hands, and a Philadelphia turkey drive named Helping Hands. None is linked to this record. Held back on purpose: no categories, audience or sources. The IRS list gives 2559 S Hobson St, 19142; not published here because it is unconfirmed. The contact name on the IRS list is not recorded.

records.name: Coalition of African Communities Philadelphia
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit working with African and Caribbean immigrants and refugees on health connections, immigration and legal help, education and culture programs, and community organizing.
records.what_you_do: Ask about volunteering or services through the site, join the mailing list, or take part in the organizing and civic engagement work.

first_step.how: Email info@africom-philly.org or join the mailing list on the site to ask about volunteering or services
first_step.basis: The site publishes a mailing list and a volunteer link, though it gives no office hours, service steps or open volunteer roles.

records.notes: Also known as AFRICOM. The IRS list spells the name Africian. No dated events or news were found; status is probably_active because the site works but is undated. The vacancies page shows no openings. Some site text looks unfinished and one footer link is malformed. No phone number is published.

records.name: Roxborough Male Chorus
records.summary: A men's choral group in Northwest Philadelphia, founded in 1922, that gives two seasonal concerts a year and sings at veterans, church, and community events.
records.what_you_do: Come to the spring or Christmas concert, or use the Contact Us link on the site to ask about joining. The site does not describe auditions.

schedule.text: Two seasonal concerts a year, a spring concert and a Christmas concert, plus performances at veterans, church, and community events. Rehearsal times are not published.

first_step.how: Come to a spring or Christmas concert, or use the Contact Us link on the site to ask how to join
first_step.basis: The site does not say how to join or audition, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Found as a lead on the RMWHS site, not in the batch. The site has no dated events; its 2026 footer is not counted. Concert venues named on the site (Leverington Presbyterian Church, the Gorgas Park veterans event) are undated. Open to public is set because the concerts are public; membership and auditions are not confirmed. Facebook and YouTube links not recorded.

records.name: 21st Ward 4th of July Association
records.summary: Runs a neighborhood Independence Day parade in Northwest Philadelphia that the group says dates back to 1831, with a park party and veterans events through the year.
records.what_you_do: Watch the July 4 parade or join a park event. To march in a parade unit, read the Participants and Parade Rules pages on the site first.

schedule.text: Independence Day parade each July 4, with a veterans tribute and picnic and a Gorgas Park party. 2027 dates are not posted yet.

locations.label: Gorgas Park (park party and veterans events)

first_step.how: Watch the July 4 parade, or email 21stward4thjuly@gmail.com to ask how to join a parade unit after reading the Participants and Parade Rules pages
first_step.basis: The site has participant and rules pages, but their contents were not in the page read, so the steps to march are unclear.

records.notes: Found as a lead on the RMWHS site. The site has photo galleries for the 2026 parade and the 2026 veterans tribute. The last_sign_of_life uses July 2026 because the parade is held on July 4. The hoagie sale, hymn sing, and veterans concert and picnic are named without dates. The Gorgas Park location comes from the site's event list; no street address is given. Facebook and YouTube links not recorded.

records.name: Grown Up Dad
records.notes: Nonprofit that produces a national PBS docuseries about fatherhood, with a Philadelphia IRS address. Its one nationwide program is Dad Collab, a $50 online peer cohort of eight dads at a time. No Philadelphia meetings or events were found, so it is marked out of area. Newest dated item is a May 2026 Telly Award. The owner may want to revisit this if online programs open to any Philadelphia resident should be listed. The site newsletter form reports a storage problem.

notes: 17 records: 12 publish, 4 out_of_area, 1 hide (private). Both WebSearch calls were used on the two IRS groups without a usable website (Roxborough Turners and Anns Helping Hand). About 22 fetches, including one 403. Roxborough Male Chorus and 21st Ward 4th of July Association were added as records because the RMWHS site named them as leads with their own websites (rule 7). Roxborough Turners and Anns Helping Hand are publish records with status unknown and no categories or sources, so they will be held back until a public source turns up. Wissahickon Sustainability Council is hidden as private and the owner may want to review that call. Guiding Stars has Foundation in its legal name but runs its own programs; treated as an operating nonprofit. Searches are fully spent; no budget was left for further lookups.
